title: Small Unmanned Aircraft System (SUAS) Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
4. MOS 7316, Small Unmanned Aircraft System (SUAS) Specialist (MGySgt to
Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. The PMOS 7316 SUAS Specialist is responsible for planning,
integrating, and executing SUAS operations in support of the Marine Air
Ground Task Force (MAGTF). 7316s integrate SUAS capabilities with unit
operations in accordance with (IAW) mission orders, scheme of maneuver, fire



                                           3-456                      Enclosure (1)
 3148                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



support coordination measures, airspace control measures, frequency
assignments, airspace, and range regulations. 7316s serve as the subject
matter expert (SME) in SUAS operations for their assigned unit.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have a five year term of enlistment.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (4) Must have normal color vision and depth perception (waiver must
be approved by an aeromedical officer).

        (5) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher (waivers may be sent to
the 7316 occupational field specialist for review and processing).

        (6) Must meet all the physical requirements of the medical screening
exam per reference (ai), the Naval Medical Department Manual, section IV,
article 15-63 for UAS. This form must be completed annually.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the requirements for the Basic Unmanned Qualification II
(BUQ-II) Course in accordance with CJCSI 3255.01 by attending the Small
Unmanned Aircraft Systems (SUAS) Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East
(M03VAN4) , Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (2) A BUQ-II individual will be awarded the PMOS 7316 after the
successful completion of the Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (SUAS)
Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East (M03VAN4) , Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (3) Upon successful completion of the Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems
(SUAS) Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East (M03VAN4), Camp Lejeune, NC and
the subsequent awarding of PMOS 7316, Small Unmanned Aircraft System
Specialists are authorized to wear the Marine Unmanned Aircraft System Breast
Insignia per MCO 1020.34.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (h), Small Unmanned Aircraft System (sUAS) Operator Training and
Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Electro-Mechanical Technicians 17-3024.

            (2) Risk Management Specialists 13-2099.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Operator, 7314.

            (2) Blackjack (MQ-21) Specialist, 8021.

            (3) Small Unmanned Aircraft System Specialist, 8623.

OFFICERS/OPERATORS 1. Introduction. The enlisted flight crews in this OccFld assist in the planning and execution of tactical in-flight refueling and assault support missions, perform navigational duties, and operate and maintain the various communications and loading equipment in transport aircraft.

4. MOS 7316, Small Unmanned Aircraft System (SUAS) Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN a. Summary. The PMOS 7316 SUAS Specialist is responsible for planning, integrating, and executing SUAS operations in support of the Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF). 7316s integrate SUAS capabilities with unit operations in accordance with (IAW) mission orders, scheme of maneuver, fire support coordination measures, airspace control measures, frequency assignments, airspace, and range regulations. 7316s serve as the subject matter expert (SME) in SUAS operations for their assigned unit. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a U.S. citizen. (2) Must have a five year term of enlistment. (3) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility. (4) Must have normal color vision and depth perception (waiver must be approved by an aeromedical officer). (5) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher (waivers may be sent to the 7316 occupational field specialist for review and processing). (6) Must meet all the physical requirements of the medical screening exam per reference (ai), the Naval Medical Department Manual, section IV, article 15-63 for UAS. This form must be completed annually. c. Requirements (1) Complete the requirements for the Basic Unmanned Qualification II (BUQ-II) Course in accordance with CJCSI 3255.01 by attending the Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (SUAS) Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East (M03VAN4) , Camp Lejeune, NC. (2) A BUQ-II individual will be awarded the PMOS 7316 after the successful completion of the Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (SUAS) Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East (M03VAN4) , Camp Lejeune, NC. (3) Upon successful completion of the Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (SUAS) Specialist Schoolhouse (SUASS) East (M03VAN4), Camp Lejeune, NC and the subsequent awarding of PMOS 7316, Small Unmanned Aircraft System Specialists are authorized to wear the Marine Unmanned Aircraft System Breast Insignia per MCO 1020.34. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (h), Small Unmanned Aircraft System (sUAS) Operator Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
